text:
Ivy: quick question about rollout degrade UX: should we distinguish "silent" vs "verbose" degrade in the console? i.e. silent = no customer-facing banner, verbose = show degrade badge + alert.
Marcus: imo yes. silent mode is useful for minor perf regressions where we want built-in fallback but not spam customers. verbose should be the default for user-visible failures.
Ellen: need to be careful: silent degrade can hide user-facing issues. ops asked for an "escalation webhook" even when silent, so teams can subscribe.
Sam: API level: add rollout.degrade_mode enum {silent, gentle, loud}. gentle = fallback but surface a small badge, loud = banner + alert + optional email.
Ivy: how do we surface triggers? can we show the top reason counts (timeout/oom/rate_limit/model_error) on the rollout card?
Marcus: yes, and include a tiny sparkline of fallback_rate. click opens a breakdown by reason. also show % of traffic affected in last 1h.
Ellen: audit proposal: any operator action that changes degrade_mode or pauses fallbacks must create an immutable audit event with fields: actor, action, before, after, justification, ts. no request bodies or outputs in the event. retention 1y.
Sam: +1. add an operator_confirm endpoint that requires justification and returns an audit_id. console attaches audit_id to the UI action.
Ivy: billing: if degrade_mode=gentle and we route to a cheaper model variant, do we bill by requested model or by the served model?
Marcus: we should bill by served model (what consumed tokens). but provide a per-rollout cost summary and a "sponsored" flag that can mark some tokens as grace/free for canary.
Ellen: operators want a briefline in invoices: "rollout r-12: 5.2k sponsored tokens". that makes reconciliation easier.
Sam: telemetry: emit decision_tag = primary|fallback|deferred plus reason. keep payload tiny. sample traces only when fallback_rate(route) > threshold OR when operator toggles "capture traces" for a rollout.
Ivy: can we allow temporary capture via console for a single incident? button: "capture traces for 10m" -> creates audit entry and flips sampling.
Marcus: implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
if (fallback_rate(route, 60s) > 0.02) {
  sampler.set(route, 0.1, ttl=600) // 10% for 10 minutes
}
// operator-capture
api.post('/rollouts/:id/capture', {duration: 600}) -> creates audit
```
Ellen: require role check for capture and operator disclosure modal: "captured traces may contain PII - will scrub outputs". default scrub = true.
Sam: retention: keep minimal decision metadata for 1y, keep sampled traces 90d. full traces require special access and an explicit justification in audit.
Ivy: what about grace abuse? someone could create rollouts repeatedly to consume sponsored tokens. suggest per-org grace quota + cooldown + visible usage history.
Marcus: agree. add grace_budget: {total_tokens, window_secs, consumed}. UI shows percent left. cooldown enforced when budget exhausted.
Ellen: operator override flow: Pause fallbacks -> requires justification, creates audit, optional 2FA if action outside business hours or affects > X tokens.
Sam: router change: attach canonical_id header for dedupe, emit attempt_index, decision_tag. billing dedupe job will reconcile charges later. feature-flag the header.
infra-bot: ticket created PLAT-6991: "degrade-modes + decision_tag + capture-traces + grace_budget" -> assigned to eng-platform, staging target Tue.
Ivy: ok next steps: Sam to spec API fields + feature flag; Marcus to mock compact rollout card with sparkline and badge; Ellen to write audit schema and retention; i'll coordinate with finance on grace accounting. sync Wed 2pm.
Marcus: will post a quick mock and a small gif.
Sam: will include proto changes and migration notes in PR.
Ellen: i'll draft audit format and share here.
Ivy: thanks everyone. thumbs up?
Marcus: :+1:
Ellen: 👍
Sam: LGTM
